ArtifactGeneration.description:
Content-derived identity of one coherent schema/function artifact pair.
It deliberately excludes the process-local publication counter: callers
learn these values from generated artifacts and can refetch them after a
deployment race.

AuthorityDescriptor.description:
Opaque server-issued consistency descriptor for one queued mutation.
Possession grants no authority; the invocation gate first resolves a live
credential and only then compares this value with its prepared authority.

@ref LLP 0039#replay-parity-and-the-authority-instance-id — this is a
  dedicated MutationRequest channel, never a ctx-answer-ledger member.

AuthorityInvalidationDispositionV1.description:
Whether the exact commit advanced the durable authorization generation.
Preview is explicit because dry-run executes the same storage plan but
intentionally rolls it back.

AuthorityMembershipStateV1.description:
The authority-relevant state of one membership row. Application-specific
roster columns and host-private provenance deliberately stay out of the
transition receipt; the subject and scope are carried separately.

@ref LLP 0240#d3-generate-the-ordinary-roster-and-role-surface — mutation
  receipts expose predecessor/successor authority state without making
  private membership metadata application-visible.

AuthorityTransitionReceiptV1.description:
One affected subject in a writer-seam membership commit. Atomic operations
such as `transferOwner` return one receipt per changed subject, all carrying
the disposition of their shared commit.

CtxAnswerLedger.description:
The ctx-answer ledger (LLP 0051 D1): the ordered answers the deterministic
ctx surface gave during one invocation. Record mode produces it; replay
mode consumes it. Reads are never ledgered — `ctx.db` reads always
re-evaluate against the executing tier's current view; the ledger pins
*answers* only. This is LLP 0043 M2's captured replay environment as a
defined channel: LLP 0008 pins the client wire to exactly
`{generatedIds, now}`; the auth fingerprint is server-retained and never
crosses the client wire.

auth_fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint of the resolved auth context the handler observed
(LLP 0043 §Auth posture). Checked at replay when present: a mismatch
surfaces `SNAPBACK_AUTH_STALE_RESULT` rather than replaying under new
authority. Server-retained (D1 wire split) — record-mode outputs leave
it unset on client-bound surfaces.

ids.description:
Every host-generated id, in answer order (LLP 0008's `generatedIds`):
`ctx.runtime.id()` answers and `ctx.db.insert` row-id generation share
one ordered sequence.

now.description: The frozen invocation clock every `ctx.runtime.now()` answered with.

version.description:
Ledger format version, versioned alongside the shared data-tier
profile (LLP 0051 D5) so pre-extension ledgers stay replayable.

FunctionAttribution.description:
Server-derived, bearer-free attribution for one app-data function
response. Wrappers may copy this value, but cannot synthesize attribution
authority when the invocation gate did not produce it.

@ref LLP 0055#audit — every resolved service-principal function response
carries the same actor/effective/grant attribution and v1 has no agent
dry-run surface.

FunctionInvocationFacts.description:
Server-derived successful-invocation facts. Keeping the generation under
a named `facts` block leaves room for additive call facts without mixing
them into handler-owned result values.

MutationServerTiming.description: Server-owned mutation phase timestamps carried by a successful response.

Receipt.description:
A retention-ring receipt (LLP 0034 §3.2): connectionless facts about
mutations and subscription lifecycle, served by the receipts snapshot and
echoed in live-subscribe/unsubscribe outputs. Privacy (§3.3): receipts
carry opaque ids, versions, table names, and reasons — never row data or
argument values.

oneOf.description:
One mutation invocation: confirmed or rejected, with the write
surface that fan-out used.

affectedTables.description:
`null` means EXPLICITLY unknown (an IbexModule handler without a
declared write set) — distinct from `[]`, no tables.

claimLedger.description:
Private settlement evidence. `None` is the fan-out projection;
the submitting authority's direct response always carries `Some`.

enqueues.description:
Jobs this confirmed mutation durably enqueued in its own
transaction (LLP 0070 first slice; 0127 decision 7's
mutation-side association). Bounded facts only — jobId, action,
availableAtMs; never argument values. Omitted when empty, and a
rejected mutation never carries one: the receipt proves what was
scheduled with the write, and its absence on a rejection is the
inspectable rollback-schedules-nothing evidence.

idMap.description:
Private lane-L id reconciliation. `Some([])` is the explicit
no-mints map; `None` means this is lane Q or a fan-out projection.

rollbackReason.description:
The diagnostic CODE only — messages may embed argument values
(§3.3 privacy). `null` on confirmed mutations.

sequenceAllocations.description:
Private sequence evidence for the submitting authority. The value
discloses prior allocation count, so fan-out projection strips it.
@ref LLP 0135#17-allocation-authority-and-information-flow — effect
  receipts carry the full counter/scope/incarnation/value tuple
  only on the submitter's receipt.

settlementLane.description: Server-observed settlement policy. Safe to retain in fan-out.

snapshotVersion.description:
`null` only when the rejected invocation could not safely read the
durable cursor; never fabricate zero from a storage failure.

oneOf.description:
Subscription lifecycle: established / disposed, on both the durable
live-query lane and the ephemeral room lane (`lane: "ephemeral"`,
which carries `bindingId`/`collection` instead of `subscriptionId`).

snapshotVersion.description:
`null` when no storage read is safe at the emission site (the
disconnect teardown path) — the honest "unknown at death" value.

SequenceAllocationFact.description:
One tentative sequence value. It is returned during handler execution but
becomes a fact only if this exact identity/value transition commits.

@ref LLP 0135#13-allocation-versus-commit-ordering-and-gap-semantics — the
  counter advance is buffered and commits or rolls back with app writes.

SettlementClaimDisposition.description:
How settlement treated one client-captured application value. Divergence
remains visible in the claimed/authoritative pair rather than becoming a
fourth disposition.

@ref LLP 0133#receipts — settlement receipts carry labeled claims, while
  fan-out projections omit their values entirely.

SettlementLane.description:
Settle-time trust policy selected by an ordinary client-attested mutation
label. The default preserves the pre-0133 queued replay contract for older
request and retained-artifact decoders.

@ref LLP 0133#the-two-settlement-lanes — the label selects replay acceptance
  or server re-derivation without granting authority.

description:
Successful `POST /mutation/{name}` response. The mutation output and its
terminal receipt are one closed, typed envelope; rejected mutations keep
using [`ErrorResponse`] with the same receipt attached by the error path.

@ref LLP 0051#d4-finish-dk-7-the-live-envelope-becomes-schema-governed — direct
  mutation results are part of the generated client-visible wire.

attribution.description:
Server-derived attribution (LLP 0055). Admitted explicitly so the
served bytes and the closed generated schema agree: the route used to
flatten this member through `FunctionResponse<T>` while the committed
`mutation.output.schema.json` did not admit it.

@ref LLP 0094#0c6-response-shape-divergences-audited-at-137dee8c-defects-not-contract — item 4: the schema-side convergence; the schema
  is generated from the envelope actually served.

authorityDescriptor.description:
The exact server-derived authority cohort that owns this settlement.
Clients persist it with the ACK proof; it grants no authority.

title: MutationResponse
